astComparison.method: Parse both LF-normalized public artifacts with Acorn ES5; omit the version declaration and the three named help assignments; assert equality of every remaining top-level node's source text.

assertions: The R24 VM forwards the complete original message unchanged.
Each request uses the expected RECRUIT or FEATURES profile.
Each request makes one simulated HTTP call with a 5000 ms timeout.
The current server classifier and canonicalizer accept the forwarded form as SYNC.
The phone returns the simulated server reply unchanged.
Each command makes one simulated HTTP call using the expected profile.
The phone returns the simulated server reply unchanged.

conclusion: An already-installed R24 client can use the core server patch without replacement. R25 updates local help text and the displayed version; it is optional for this server patch.
reproduction: Run an in-memory Node module with node --import tsx --input-type=module from the repository root; no temporary source or artifact files are required.

Read the baseline public artifact with git show 0c188785:integrations/messengerbot-r/v1-strict/KLOL_KAKAO_BOT_V1_STRICT_MESSENGERBOT_R.js and read the current public artifact; compare their non-help/non-version Acorn nodes as described above.

Extract only makeRuntime, evaluate and replyFor from tests/kakao-v1-strict-messengerbot.test.mjs. Do not execute the test file's builder test. Instantiate its simulated Java/Jsoup VM with the baseline R24 source.

Generate synthetic current forms using v1StrictPartyDetailReply and inhouseCopyFormReply, add the two old name-only inhouse scenarios, apply the listed prefixes and line endings, then assert forwarding, profile, timeout, reply and current canonical SYNC behavior. Check the four detail/finish commands separately.
recordingNote: Recorded from the already-completed 70-case run without rerunning the checks.
